feature: A clip's own sound is the bottom half of the clip
summary: A recording with sound is now one clip on its video track: the picture on top, the waveform underneath, one outline. The separate V1 sound row is gone. Detach Audio still moves the sound to an Audio track, and Re-attach Audio puts it back inside the clip.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording with sound.

try.do: Open a recording with sound and look at V1: one clip, picture over waveform, and an empty Audio track under it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the waveform half: the clip is picked, with one ring round both halves.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the clip's right edge in by a second, from either half: picture and sound end together.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press B and click the waveform half: one cut goes through both halves.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right click V1's header and choose Mute Sound: the waveform dims and a slashed speaker appears on the half.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right click the waveform half and choose Detach Audio: the sound moves to the Audio track and the clip becomes picture only.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right click the sound on Audio and choose Re-attach Audio: it goes back inside the clip.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does a recording now read as one thing rather than two rows you have to keep in your head?
Is an even split of picture and sound right, or should the picture get more of the height?
Is the empty Audio track under a recording useful as the place for music, or would you rather it stayed away until you need it?
Is Mute Sound easy enough to find on the track header's right-click menu, the Track menu and the Audio section, or do you want a switch on the header?
Can you still set the volume by dragging the line in the half, or is it too fine?
rough: Grown-up tool check: Final Cut draws attached audio inside the clip, Premiere links two items across tracks. Photonz follows Final Cut here because that is your call on 2026-11-05. Before: 2026-10-13-sound-under-its-video-0-opened.png. After: the first picture above.

The video mocks now draw the sound inside the clip, changed as you asked on 2026-11-05. 2026-11-06-clip-sound-inside-mock-and-app.png has the mock over the app. The mock's waveform is bars and its clip colours are its own, your call on 2026-11-05 covers the drawing.
The timeline stands 28 points taller for a recording than before, because the clip is 56 points and the empty Audio track stays under it. A timeline with many tracks scrolls sooner.
The volume line has 17 points of travel in the half, where the old row gave 23. It is coarser under the hand; taller rows or the Audio section's slider give finer control.
The strip that takes a press along the volume line is narrower on the half, so a drag near the line still moves the clip. A sideways drag right on the line changes nothing, as it did on the old row.
Mute and Solo for a clip's sound have no switch on the track header, only menus and the Audio section. The header's Solo and Lock are the track's; Lock now covers picture and sound together.

Deleting the only Audio track takes what is on it, then an empty Audio track comes back to wait, the way a silent recording's always has. So under a recording you cannot get rid of the last empty Audio track.
